overview:
Our research broadly focuses on social stress and resilience factors among people with or at risk for chronic health conditions. We have particular interest in the impact of stigma and discrimination in driving health outcomes and inequities. This involves examination of immediate and long-term effects of stigma on mental health, health behavior, healthcare engagement, clinical outcomes, and wellbeing. We also study the community and structural contexts in which these relationships occur. We predominantly use mixed methods approaches to answer our research questions.

We are interested in moving this research forward to development, evaluation, and implementation of interventions in healthcare and community settings that will diminish stigma and bolster social support. We are currently adapting health programs that will be delivered in primary and specialty care setting involving a care partner. We also evaluate the systemic intervention of the Primary Care Behavioral Health (PCBH) model in delivering whole-person, collaborative healthcare.
